s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of painful vision loss with lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Blurred vision and loss of vision in the left lower quadrant
Vitreous haze and optic-nerve pallor in the left eye
key_facts: 63-year-old white man
3-week history of redness of the left eye
Extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy
Blurred vision and loss of vision in the left lower quadrant
Supraorbital pain in both eyes
No fever, chills, weight loss, rash, or joint pains
Several weeks of malaise
Initial treatment with erythromycin ointment, topical prednisolone, tobramycin/dexamethasone ointment, and cyclopentolate without improvement
Visual acuity 20/20 in the right eye and 20/125 in the left
Intraocular pressure 11 mm Hg in the right eye and 32 mm Hg in the left
Slit-lamp examination showed 1+ cell in the right eye, 4+ cell in the left
Gelatinous layered hypopyon with red-blood-cell layering in both eyes
Dilated exam revealed 1+ vitreous haze and optic-nerve pallor in the left eye
B-scan ultrasonography showed no retinal detachment or masses
Acellular, dense, proteinaceous material on anterior chamber paracentesis

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy and intraocular findings suggestive of malignancy

shortlist.label: Intraocular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Acellular, dense, proteinaceous material on anterior chamber paracentesis and panuveitis

shortlist.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
shortlist.why_kept: Panuveitis and lymphadenopathy, with possible systemic involvement

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral lymphadenopathy and granulomatous uveitis, consistent with systemic disease

shortlist.label: Sympathetic ophthalmia
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral eye involvement with panuveitis and possible autoimmune etiology

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with panuveitis, extensive bilateral lymphadenopathy, and a gelatinous layered hypopyon with red-blood-cell layering in both eyes, along with the presence of acellular, dense, proteinaceous material on anterior chamber paracentesis, is highly suggestive of intraocular lymphoma, a type of cancer that can cause these specific ocular and systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma could explain the lymphadenopathy, it is less specific to the ocular findings described.

rejected.label: Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with granulomatous uveitis, skin, and hair findings, which are not mentioned in the vignette.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis often presents with granulomatous uveitis and other systemic findings such as lung involvement, which are not described in the case.

rejected.label: Sympathetic ophthalmia
rejected.why: This is a rare, bilateral granulomatous uveitis following penetrating eye injury, which is not indicated in the patient's history.
